---
title: "Datasets"
subtitle: "The data files the slides read, where each one comes from, and how it was prepared"
---

The decks read their data from
[`materials/data/`](https://github.com/EBukin/mk68-2023-24-public/tree/main/materials/data).
Every file there is a cleaned extract; the scripts that produced them are in
[`data-raw/`](https://github.com/EBukin/mk68-2023-24-public/tree/main/data-raw),
next to a note on the source. The raw downloads themselves are not in the
repository. The `.rds` files open in R with `readr::read_rds()` or
`readRDS()`.

Several examples use datasets shipped with R packages rather than files; those
are listed at the end.

## Provenance

### Nutrition surveys (Congo, Brazil, Burkina Faso) {#nutrition}

Individual food consumption surveys shared through the
[FAO/WHO GIFT](https://www.fao.org/gift-individual-food-consumption/data-and-indicator/en/)
platform (Global Individual Food consumption data Tool). Prepared by
[`congo-consumption.R`](https://github.com/EBukin/mk68-2023-24-public/blob/main/data-raw/congo-consumption.R),
[`brazil-food-consumption.R`](https://github.com/EBukin/mk68-2023-24-public/blob/main/data-raw/brazil-food-consumption.R)
and
[`burkin-faso-consumption.R`](https://github.com/EBukin/mk68-2023-24-public/blob/main/data-raw/burkin-faso-consumption.R):
the consumption file is joined to the subject file and summed to daily intake
per subject.

The contributors ask to be acknowledged whenever the data or its derivatives
are presented:

-   **Burkina Faso** (BFA-00001): Institut de Recherche pour le Développement
    (IRD); Institut de Recherche en Sciences de la Santé (IRSS); HarvestPlus,
    International Food Policy Research Institute (IFPRI), 2016, "The 2010 Food
    consumption and iron status survey in two provinces of rural Burkina
    Faso", doi:10.7910/DVN/5CXCLX.
-   **Democratic Republic of the Congo** (COD-00091): University of Colorado
    School of Medicine, Anschutz Medical Campus and their collaborators in
    Kinshasa; Sud-Ubangi, Democratic Republic of the Congo; 2014/2016; Women
    First Dietary Recall Data.

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
## A known quirk of the Congo file

`congo-consumption.R` reads the Congo consumption file but joins it to the
**Burkina Faso** subject file (line 14 of the script). The country and region
columns of `congo-nutrition.rds` therefore read "Burkina Faso" and its
provinces, and the subject attributes (sex, age, weight, height) come from that
survey too, while the nutrient columns are from the Congo survey. The slides use
only the nutrient columns.
:::

### World income distribution {#income-distribution}

Lakner and Milanovic's global income distribution, as made available to Our
World in Data and published on
[Max Roser's website](https://www.maxroser.com/roser/graphs/WorldIncomeDistribution_LaknerAndMilanovic/WorldIncomeDistribution_LaknerAndMilanovic1988_100.html).
The data up to 2008 accompany Lakner and Milanovic (2015), *Global Income
Distribution: From the Fall of the Berlin Wall to the Great Recession*, World
Bank. The JSON series were saved from the website's console and parsed by
[`income-distribution.R`](https://github.com/EBukin/mk68-2023-24-public/blob/main/data-raw/income-distribution.R);
the six yearly folders of raw series are in
[`data-raw/income-distribution/`](https://github.com/EBukin/mk68-2023-24-public/tree/main/data-raw/income-distribution).

### WHO child growth standards {#who}

The [length/height-for-age](https://www.who.int/tools/child-growth-standards/standards/length-height-for-age)
z-score expanded tables for boys and girls from the WHO Child Growth Standards,
stacked by
[`who.R`](https://github.com/EBukin/mk68-2023-24-public/blob/main/data-raw/who.R).

### UN World Population Prospects {#un-population}

Population on 1 January by single age and sex, medium variant, from the
[UN World Population Prospects 2022](https://population.un.org/wpp/Download/Standard/Population/),
filtered to 1960, 1990 and 2020 by
[`un-population.R`](https://github.com/EBukin/mk68-2023-24-public/blob/main/data-raw/un-population.R).
The raw download was too large to keep.

### The Datasaurus Dozen {#datasaurus}

From Matejka and Fitzmaurice (2017), *Same Stats, Different Graphs*
([Autodesk Research](https://www.autodesk.com/research/publications/same-stats-different-graphs)),
via Alberto Cairo's
[Download the Datasaurus](http://www.thefunctionalart.com/2016/08/download-datasaurus-never-trust-summary.html).

### CFC-11 at Mauna Loa {#cfc11}

Monthly mean CFC-11 (F11) mixing ratios by station from the NOAA Global
Monitoring Laboratory's HATS programme,
[gml.noaa.gov](https://gml.noaa.gov/aftp/data/hats/cfcs/cfc11/combined/HATS_global_F11.txt).

### Not in the repository

Two files the decks read are deliberately excluded by the `.gitignore`:

-   `materials/data/poverty-population.csv`, a country-level extract of extreme
    poverty rates and population used for the weighted-mean example in Week 1,
    Part 2. The slide credits
    [Our World in Data](https://ourworldindata.org/extreme-poverty) and the
    World Bank's [Poverty and Inequality Platform](https://pip.worldbank.org/home).
-   `data-raw/uganda-poject/Uganda_B_E_agri and nutrition 04.06.2018.sav`,
    the baseline and endline survey of the Uganda nutrition project used for
    the scatter-plot section of Week 3 (Jordan et al., 2022, *Foods* 11(3):344,
    [doi:10.3390/foods11030344](https://doi.org/10.3390/foods11030344)).
    [`uganda-poject.R`](https://github.com/EBukin/mk68-2023-24-public/blob/main/data-raw/uganda-poject.R)
    explores its variable dictionary.

Two further scripts in `data-raw/` are not used by any deck:
[`read-geojson.R`](https://github.com/EBukin/mk68-2023-24-public/blob/main/data-raw/read-geojson.R)
(parses `SO_geojson_2020_A.json`) and
[`summarystata.R`](https://github.com/EBukin/mk68-2023-24-public/blob/main/data-raw/summarystata.R)
(helper for cleaning `skimr` summaries). The `progressa/` folder holds a
PROGRESA extract with a variable list, taken from a
[public replication repository](https://github.com/snehavcs/Progresa-Analysis-Econometrics),
and `cambodia/` a pointer to a
[PLOS ONE article](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0150750);
neither is read by the current decks.

## Datasets from R packages

| Dataset | Package | Used in |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `penguins` | [palmerpenguins](https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/) | Week 3: bi-variate data, scatter plots, correlation matrix |
| `UN11` | [alr4](https://cran.r-project.org/package=alr4) | Week 3: correlation and causation (life expectancy and fertility) |
| `RiceFarms` | [plm](https://cran.r-project.org/package=plm) | Week 3: rice yields and fertiliser; Week 7: production function |
| `sleep` | base R (`datasets`) | Week 5: one-sample t-test |
| `gomez.splitsplit` | [agridat](https://cran.r-project.org/package=agridat) | Week 6: t-test recap |
| `fuel2001` | [alr4](https://cran.r-project.org/package=alr4) | Week 6: multiple regression example |
| `MinnLand` | [alr4](https://cran.r-project.org/package=alr4) | Week 7: hedonic land prices |

: {tbl-colwidths="[22,22,56]"}

The sampling, confidence-interval and simple-regression sections simulate their
populations in the slides themselves, with fixed seeds.
